positioning.audienceAppeal: People who feel not represented, restricted, and ready for change.

forbidden: Do not introduce unlisted font families.
Do not use generic default typefaces as final output.
Do not substitute fonts without a validation warning.

usage: Use official CCC logo assets only.
Use brand colors or in-paper colors depending on the template.
Do not redraw, distort, recolor outside the palette, or invent alternate marks.

guidance: Keep the message short and direct.
Use geometric blocks, bands, and sharp-edged shapes.
Do not create off-palette gradients or decorative effects.

notes: Brand guide pages use warm white backgrounds, deep navy headings, and a pale outlined CCC monogram as a background motif.
Social examples rely on hard-edged geometric blocks, high contrast navy/orange fields, compact all-caps labels, and a visible CCC mark.
Document templates use precise margins, hierarchy callouts, and restrained topic-specific graphics; policy memos explicitly prohibit visual elements.

styleVariants.useFor: Petition, policymaker, lawmaker, mandate, and direct advocacy ask posts
styleVariants.composition: Reference 3 system: high-urgency Autumn Orange layout with the original Montserrat Bold headline slots, selected Leila text blocks, real megaphone paths, dark action band, dark footer, official orange logo, and a cropped gradient CCC mark.

styleVariants.useFor: Policy alerts, lawmaker calls, urgent petition posts
styleVariants.composition: Reference 3 system: Autumn Orange field, tilted issue label, original Montserrat Bold hierarchy, selected Leila text blocks, real megaphone paths, dark action band and footer, official orange logo, and a cropped marigold-to-transparent CCC mark.
Reference 2 system: Leila field, monumental Autumn Orange Anton statistic, bold supporting statement, compact evidence callout, bottom logo, and a cropped gradient CCC mark.

Reference 4 system: controlled Leila/Warm White split, paired Anton BAD/GOOD or NO/YES headlines, compact comparison cards, one tertiary accent at most, footer URL, official logo, and cropped gradient CCC marks.

styleVariants.useFor: Attributed quotes from approved CCC team members
styleVariants.composition: Reference 5 system: exact supplied quote template with a deep-night field, official top-left logo, cropped CCC mark, protected Anton quote and Montserrat Bold attribution zone, mandatory Autumn Orange emphasis, and one fully embedded approved portrait contained without cropping and scaled proportionally to quote length below the text zone.

socialPosts.referenceUsage: Packaged SVG post references are locked layout contracts. Preserve their coordinates, native display fonts, line rhythm, crop behavior, CCC mark geometry, icon paths, CTA placement, logo usage, and variant structure while replacing their wording with the requested message.
composition: Map navy_poster to reference 1, statistic_card to reference 2, petition_push/orange_alert to reference 3, contrast_cards to reference 4, and quote_post to reference 5.
Use each reference's native display face and fixed type slots: Anton Regular in references 1, 2, 4, and 5; Montserrat Bold in reference 3. Never use SVG textLength stretching.
Use the actual nested-C CCC mark silhouette as a large cropped background element; fill it with a subtle approved gradient and never approximate it with concentric circles.
Prefer one dominant field color with text blocks, strips, underlines, or compact callout chips; a controlled two-field split is reserved for contrast_cards because reference 4 uses it.
For dark layouts, use Leila as the dominant background, Warm White typography, Autumn Orange emphasis, and a subtle Slate Blue-to-transparent CCC mark.
For orange alert layouts, use Autumn Orange as the dominant background with stacked Leila text boxes, Base White typography, and a dark footer band.
For petition, policymaker, lawmaker, and mandate asks, default to petition_push or orange_alert rather than navy_poster.
Create variety by choosing among the six reference-mapped style variants; do not invent crop or coordinate variations inside a locked reference layout.
Keep layouts poster-like and direct rather than decorative or editorial.
Avoid full-height diagonal split compositions, serif display typography, large unrelated comparison panels, soft gradients, bokeh, generic stock styling, and off-palette effects.
forbiddenComposition: Do not use large left/right split-screen fields except for the reference-4 contrast_cards system.
Do not use full-height diagonal divider wedges as the primary composition.
Do not use serif headline typography.
Do not create placeholder logo boxes for final output.
Do not imitate a generic policy comparison infographic when the guide calls for bold CCC poster cards.

onePagers.referenceUsage: The two populated one-pager SVGs are visual references only. Generated one-pagers must begin from the MCP-provided clean working shell, which removes all original text and raster images while preserving the reference canvas, section boundaries, coordinates, typography hierarchy, brush shapes, normalized arrows, card geometry, background mark, footer, and logo geometry.

templates.titleStyle: large left-column Anton uppercase title with selected Autumn Orange lines
templates.illustrationGrammar: One large photorealistic central consumer object or cutaway composite, surrounded by three related material/component cutouts, connected with the reference orange circular arrow and white dashed pointers.

templates.label: Access and regulatory barriers
templates.useFor: Permits, approvals, restrictions, access, safety, health, availability, bureaucracy, and issues where rules block use of a beneficial product or service.
templates.titleStyle: large left-column Anton Regular uppercase title with a single Autumn Orange keyword or line
templates.illustrationGrammar: One large photorealistic central object, building, device, or cutaway composite, with three context-specific regulatory callouts and simple outlined policy icons in the fixed reference positions.

lockedElements: 1186.51 by 1535.49 viewBox and page aspect ratio
deep-night upper field and warm-white evidence field
cropped CCC watermark geometry and opacity
headline origin, width, hierarchy, line rhythm, and template-specific display style
orange brush panels, connector arrows, dashed rules, icon circles, and dividers
lead-stat panel, bridge statement, lower-section heading, evidence-card grid, conclusion panel, source line, and logo placement
all margins, section boundaries, corner radii, stroke weights, and alignment
mutableElements: headline and deck copy fitted to the existing slots
three policy callout headings and supporting bullets
bridge statement, lower-section heading, conclusion, and source citations
central contextual object illustration and its supporting component/callout cutouts only
illustrationRules: Use only the clean working SVG returned by create_one_pager; never append new content to the populated visual reference.
The clean shell must contain no original text or raster images, and the final file must preserve data-ccc-clean-template="mutable-content-cleared-v1".
Generate the physical object most directly connected to the policy context, not an abstract metaphor.
Match the references' photorealistic editorial cutout/cutaway style on a transparent background with crisp edges.
Use exactly one dominant self-contained central object composite; any supporting cutouts must be included within that transparent composite rather than added as loose overlapping images.
Preserve the original illustration boxes, scale hierarchy, and connector positions; do not move text to accommodate an image.
Never overlap illustrations with headline, callout, statistic, conclusion, source, or logo text.
Embed every raster illustration directly in the SVG as a base64 data:image URI through SVG 1.1 xlink:href; never leave external file links or use the browser-oriented SVG 2 href attribute.

Every downloadable SVG must declare the Illustrator SVG 1.1 export contract, keep editable text assigned to packaged locally installed CCC fonts, inline vector logos, and avoid data:font web-font embedding and live SVG filters.
Do not use generic AI scenes, painterly artwork, 3D blobs, floating circles, background photography, or unrelated stock icons.
componentLayoutRules: Use one font family and one weight consistently for every repeated component role.
Every text-bearing component must declare data-ccc-component, data-ccc-bounds, and data-ccc-text-inset.
Every text-bearing component must also declare a measured data-ccc-text-safe-box contained inside its component bounds; text may not extend outside that box or into another component.

Every visible text line must be a direct x/y-positioned text element inside a real data-ccc-component group; hidden placeholder roles, transformed text, tspans, textLength, and lengthAdjust are forbidden.
The validator measures rendered text boxes and rejects text-to-text or text-to-illustration overlap even when component metadata claims the layout is safe.
Keep at least a 24-unit gutter between component bounds; components may not touch or overlap.
Align text to a shared inset and baseline grid inside each brush panel, card, callout, banner, and takeaway box.

Build each connector as a tangent-aligned double-ended arrow: one clean 3-unit shaft, 6 7 dash rhythm, and two compact filled vector arrowheads that physically meet the shaft. Do not use SVG marker-start, marker-mid, or marker-end, and never cross a text-safe box.

strictGenerationRules: Use only colors listed in this brand data.
Use only listed typography families and weights.
Use packaged official SVG logo assets by default; if unavailable, draft mode may leave a placeholder and final mode must fail validation.
Do not invent gradients, shadows, illustrations, icons, or textures outside the brand guide; the only default gradient is the semi-transparent fill inside the cropped CCC mark watermark.
Prefer sharp geometric vector shapes, strong contrast, and concise text.

For social posts, follow the mapped reference system with its native display font, small issue label, official logo, footer URL, real reference icon paths, and the cropped nested-C CCC mark filled with a subtle transparent brand gradient.
For petition, policymaker, lawmaker, mandate, and direct advocacy asks, default to petition_push or orange_alert rather than a generic navy poster.
Vary social post layouts across navy poster, petition push, orange alert, statistic card, and compact contrast-card variants based on the message.

Treat the packaged SVG post references as locked layout contracts: preserve coordinates, native display fonts, line rhythm, crop behavior, CCC mark geometry, icon paths, CTA placement, and logo usage while replacing the wording.

For one-pagers, call create_one_pager, open its linked source SVG, duplicate that exact file, and preserve at least 90% of its measured vector geometry; only replace fitted copy and the contextual central/supporting object illustrations.
Never validate an 1186.51x1535.49 one-pager only as a generic SVG artifact; it must pass validate_one_pager_svg, including source-template geometry retention.

One-pager contextual objects must be photorealistic transparent-background editorial cutouts or cutaways, embedded in the SVG, contained inside the original illustration zones, and kept clear of every text region.
Generate every social post through create_social_svg and require data-ccc-layout-lock=reference-exact; legacy or freeform social renderers are forbidden.

Fit large social headlines into the native reference slots without SVG textLength, lengthAdjust, font-stretch, or non-uniform scale transforms; references 1, 2, 4, and 5 use Anton Regular, while reference 3 uses Montserrat Bold.

When rasterizing a social SVG, explicitly load the packaged files in assets/fonts and verify the rendered headline is Anton or Montserrat Bold as mapped; never deliver a PNG produced with a silent serif or system-font fallback.
Do not use serif display headlines or full-height diagonal divider wedges; use a large split only for the reference-4 contrast_cards system.
For social posts, default to 1080x1350 unless the user explicitly asks for another brand-supported size.
For policy memos, do not add decorative visual elements.
Return validation warnings before final creative output whenever required assets or fonts are missing.
